scope.heading: What am I being assessed on?

flashcards.back: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. Energy is released.

flashcards.front: Anaerobic respiration in muscles: word equation
flashcards.back: glucose → lactic acid. Less energy is released than in aerobic respiration.

flashcards.front: Anaerobic respiration in yeast (fermentation): word equation
flashcards.back: glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide.

flashcards.front: Where in the cell does aerobic respiration happen?
flashcards.back: In the mitochondria.
The windpipe. It carries air from the mouth and nose down to the lungs. Rings of cartilage keep it open.
The trachea splits into two bronchi, one for each lung. These branch into smaller tubes called bronchioles.
Tiny air sacs at the end of the bronchioles. Gas exchange happens here.
A sheet of muscle under the lungs. It contracts and flattens when you breathe in.

flashcards.front: What happens when you breathe in?
flashcards.back: The diaphragm contracts and flattens. The rib muscles pull the ribs up and out. The chest gets bigger, pressure falls, and air moves in.
Oxygen diffuses from the air in the alveoli into the blood. Carbon dioxide diffuses from the blood into the alveoli.

flashcards.front: How are alveoli adapted for gas exchange?
flashcards.back: Large surface area, walls only one cell thick, and a good blood supply.
A column. Elements in the same group have similar properties.
A row, going across the table.
Metals are on the left and in the middle. Non-metals are on the right.
Shiny, good conductors of heat and electricity, can be bent or hammered into shape (malleable), and most have high melting points.
Dull, poor conductors of heat and electricity, and brittle when solid. Many are gases at room temperature.
Soft metals with low density. They react with water to make hydrogen and an alkaline solution. They get more reactive going down the group.
Very unreactive gases. Boiling point increases going down the group. Examples: helium, neon, argon.

flashcards.front: Why are group 1 metals stored in oil?
flashcards.back: To stop them reacting with oxygen and water in the air.
A scientist who arranged the elements in a table in 1869. He left gaps for elements that had not been discovered yet.
Like poles repel (north and north, or south and south). Unlike poles attract (north and south).
Iron, nickel and cobalt. Steel is magnetic because it contains iron.
The area around a magnet where it has an effect. Field lines go from the north pole to the south pole.

flashcards.front: Where is a magnetic field strongest?
flashcards.back: At the poles, where the field lines are closest together.
A coil of wire with an electric current flowing through it, usually wrapped around an iron core. It is magnetic only when the current is on.

flashcards.front: Three ways to make an electromagnet stronger
flashcards.back: More turns on the coil, a bigger current, and an iron core.
Scrapyard cranes, electric bells, door locks and relays.
A small magnet that lines up with the Earth's magnetic field. It can be used to plot field lines.

quiz.q: What are the products of aerobic respiration?
quiz.explain: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water.

quiz.q: What is made in muscles during anaerobic respiration?
quiz.explain: In muscles, glucose → lactic acid.

quiz.q: Where does gas exchange happen in the lungs?
quiz.explain: Gas exchange happens in the tiny air sacs called alveoli.

quiz.q: What does the diaphragm do when you breathe in?
quiz.explain: The diaphragm contracts and flattens, so the chest gets bigger.

quiz.q: Which part of the cell does aerobic respiration happen in?
quiz.explain: Mitochondria are where aerobic respiration happens.

quiz.q: Which gas moves from the alveoli into the blood?
quiz.explain: Oxygen diffuses into the blood. Carbon dioxide diffuses out.

quiz.q: What does yeast make during anaerobic respiration?
quiz.explain: Yeast makes ethanol and carbon dioxide. This is called fermentation.

quiz.q: Which is NOT an adaptation of the alveoli?
quiz.explain: Alveoli have very thin walls so gases can pass through quickly.

quiz.q: What is a column in the periodic table called?
quiz.explain: Columns are groups. Rows are periods.

quiz.q: Where are the metals in the periodic table?
options: On the left and in the middle
quiz.explain: Metals are on the left and in the middle. Non-metals are on the right.

quiz.q: Which is a property of most metals?
quiz.explain: Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity.

quiz.q: What gas is made when a group 1 metal reacts with water?
quiz.explain: Group 1 metal + water → metal hydroxide + hydrogen.

quiz.q: What happens to the reactivity of group 1 metals going down the group?
quiz.explain: Potassium is more reactive than sodium, and sodium is more reactive than lithium.

quiz.q: Why are noble gases (group 0) used in light bulbs and signs?
quiz.explain: Noble gases are very unreactive, so they are safe to use.

quiz.q: Which element is a noble gas?
quiz.explain: Neon is in group 0, with helium and argon.

quiz.q: Why did Mendeleev leave gaps in his periodic table?
options: For elements that had not been discovered yet
Because he did not like some elements
quiz.explain: His gaps were later filled by new elements with the properties he predicted.

quiz.q: What happens when two north poles are put together?
quiz.explain: Like poles repel. Unlike poles attract.

quiz.q: Which of these is a magnetic material?
quiz.explain: Iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic.

quiz.q: Which way do magnetic field lines point?
options: They do not have a direction
quiz.explain: Field lines go from the north pole to the south pole.

quiz.q: Which would make an electromagnet stronger?
quiz.explain: More turns, more current and an iron core make it stronger.

quiz.q: What is one advantage of an electromagnet over a permanent magnet?
options: It can be switched on and off
It is always the same strength
quiz.explain: An electromagnet is only magnetic when the current flows.

quiz.q: Which is a use of an electromagnet?
quiz.explain: Scrapyard cranes switch the magnet on to lift steel and off to drop it.

quiz.q: Where is the magnetic field of a bar magnet strongest?
quiz.explain: Field lines are closest together at the poles.
